# EDTF value

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:edtfValue`](gmeow-edtfValue.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/edtfValue>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/temporal`](../../slices/temporal.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

An ISO 8601-2 (EDTF) expression of an instant or interval, stored as a plain literal. EDTF parsing and normalization are solver-layer concerns ([Principle 12](https://github.com/Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-ontology/blob/main/CONSTITUTION.md#principle-12)).

## Structure

**Property shape:** datatype property; `?` -> [`rdfs:Literal`](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Literal); functional

Use [`gmeow:edtfValue`](gmeow-edtfValue.md) from `?` to [`rdfs:Literal`](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Literal) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use when a point or span is approximate, uncertain, seasonal, or open-ended — '1804?', '19XX', '2020-21/2020-09' — and a single crisp [xsd:dateTime](http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime) would lie about the precision.

### Avoid when

- Avoid when a fully crisp value is known (use [`gmeow:instantValue`](gmeow-instantValue.md)) and avoid encoding ontic determinacy here instead of on [`gmeow:hasDeterminacy`](gmeow-hasDeterminacy.md); the EDTF string expresses the value, not its determinacy classification.

### How to use

- Store the raw EDTF string as a plain literal and leave parsing, range expansion, and comparison to the solver layer (P12); pair with [`gmeow:hasDeterminacy`](gmeow-hasDeterminacy.md) to make the approximate/uncertain nature queryable without parsing.

### Examples

- ex:foundingInstant [`gmeow:edtfValue`](gmeow-edtfValue.md) "1804?".
